$comment: Presets for the Mini Particle Simulator.
Toolchain is selected by COMPILER NAME (gcc/g++, clang/clang++, or cl for MSVC) resolved
from PATH, so there are no machine-specific absolute paths and these work wherever the
toolchain lives. Have the toolchain (and the generator's tool) on PATH before invoking:
- gcc-*   : run from an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell
- clang-* : run from an MSYS2 CLANG64 shell
- msvc-vs : Visual Studio generator, multi-config, NO dev prompt needed (emits a .sln)
Generator: Ninja by default; the *-make presets fall back to MinGW Makefiles (gcc/clang),
and msvc-vs omits the generator so CMake auto-selects the newest installed Visual Studio.
Usage:  cmake --preset gcc-debug then cmake --build --preset gcc-debug
cmake --preset msvc-vs then cmake --build --preset msvc-vs-debug  (config chosen at build time)

configurePresets.name: base
$comment: Common ground for every preset. No generator and no compiler here: those come from the
generator bases (ninja/make) and toolchain bases (gcc/clang) that concrete presets combine
via multiple inheritance.
binaryDir keys on ${presetName} so each toolchain/buildtype/generator combo gets its own tree.
CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON writes compile_commands.json for clangd/IDE include resolution.

configurePresets.name: ninja
configurePresets.$comment: Generator base: Ninja (preferred, parallel by default). 'ninja' must be on PATH.

configurePresets.name: make
configurePresets.$comment: Generator base: MinGW Makefiles, the fallback when Ninja isn't installed. Finds 'mingw32-make' on PATH.

configurePresets.name: gcc
$comment: Toolchain base: GCC, found by name on PATH (no absolute paths).
Run from a shell with the UCRT64 bin on PATH so g++, windres, and the runtime DLLs resolve
(windres needs its companion GCC preprocessor on PATH, see PROGRESS-GPU Session 14).

configurePresets.name: clang
configurePresets.$comment: Toolchain base: Clang, found by name on PATH. Run from a shell with the CLANG64 bin on PATH.

configurePresets.name: gcc-debug
configurePresets.$comment: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug drives the $<CONFIG:Debug> generator expressions in CMakeLists (flags + ENABLE_DEBUG_LAYER).

configurePresets.name: gcc-debug-make
configurePresets.$comment: Same as gcc-debug but with the MinGW Makefiles generator, for systems without Ninja.

configurePresets.name: msvc-vs
configurePresets.description: Zero setup MSVC: CMake auto-selects the newest installed Visual Studio and emits a .sln. Multi-config, choose Debug/Release at build time via msvc-vs-debug / msvc-vs-release.
$comment: No 'generator' field on purpose. A VS generator name is version-locked ('Visual Studio
17 2022' vs 'Visual Studio 18 2026' vs future releases), so hardcoding one fails on any
machine with a different VS installed. Omitting it lets CMake's default-generator logic
pick the newest installed Visual Studio automatically, which is hopefully version-agnostic.
Visual Studio is a multi-config generator, sp CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE is intentionally not set here;
the config is chosen at build time by the build/workflow presets. No Developer Command
Prompt needed, the generator locates MSVC via vswhere.

workflowPresets.name: clang-debug
workflowPresets.$comment: configure -> build for the Clang Debug (Ninja) config: cmake --workflow --preset clang-debug

workflowPresets.name: clang-release
workflowPresets.$comment: configure -> build for the Clang Release (Ninja) config: cmake --workflow --preset clang-release

workflowPresets.name: gcc-debug
workflowPresets.$comment: configure -> build for the GCC Debug (Ninja) config: cmake --workflow --preset gcc-debug

workflowPresets.name: gcc-release
workflowPresets.$comment: configure -> build for the GCC Release (Ninja) config: cmake --workflow --preset gcc-release

workflowPresets.name: msvc-vs-debug
workflowPresets.$comment: MSVC via the Visual Studio generator, Debug config (no dev prompt needed).

workflowPresets.name: msvc-vs-release
workflowPresets.$comment: MSVC via the Visual Studio generator, Release config (no dev prompt needed).
